selections.comment: Kdeux Saint Fray was well held in a Grade 2 at Cheltenham in January, but should put up a bold showing in this company. However, the maiden hurdle he won at Catterick hasn't worked out and he's taken on with returning C&D winner THE BLUESMAN. Open to any amount of improvement on his second start after wind surgery, the Paul Nicholls-trained six-year-old, who also won a bumper here last April, is a most appealing novice to be competing at this time of year. Lieutenant Mayne completes the shortlist.

selections.comment: The most interesting one is Bobby Joe Leg who races off a mark of 48 now back on turf having raced off 71 last time at Southwell on Tapeta. While undoubtedly better suited to the artificail surfaces he has rarely gone on turf since his 4yo days. Maxine Carr's gelding is feared but on balance opposed. Amayretto looks to have every chance if wound up for her return off a pound lower mark than her sole win which came on fast ground. Fitness has to be taken on trust and there's a slight concern that 7f here might just be on the sharp side so BELTANE gets the vote. He ended last term with three placed efforts in his last four runs, all in class 5 handicaps 7f-8f, and while a bit below par on his season bow there'll be no rust today and eased back to this lower grade is fancied to track the pace and pounce late on. Prefer The Sister is another eased in grade and needs considering

selections.comment: LAST SHAMARDAL deserves compensation for a defeat last time having looked the winner everyhwhere but the line. The drop back to 7f may help given how sweetly Jack Channon's gelding travelled over the mile last time and he won convincingly over a sharp 7f prior to his latest narrow defeat. He can cope with the slight step up in class and will be tough to beat if taking to the likely faster ground. Singoura is the obvious danger. She won on second start last time improving on her debut with a smooth win at Southwell over 7f. A mark of 75 looks more than fair given her potential and if she can translate her AW form to turf will go close. Frankies Dream has won four and been second five times in his last eleven runs and is still steadily improving. Both turf runs have been in keeping with his AW best, and if anything they rate a bit higher so if finding any more for the step up in trip poses a potent threat to all

selections.comment: Two to take the eye both opened their accounts in maiden company last time with Alondra taking a Southwell sprint and Acrisius a Brighton maiden on quick ground. Both should give another good account with Mick Easterby's gelding feared most given what looks a lenient opening mark of 73 and having shown a liking already to quick ground. The 236 day layoff is a slight concern and it's worth keeping an eye on any market activity. Both can go close but FIORELLA PRONCESS may have their measure. A fine third last time when being touched off by the slenderest of margins (beaten a nose and nose again by first two) she's proven her worth in handicap company and looks ultra-dependable. The switch back to turf is no issue as she went down by just half a length on career debut on fast ground here over 5f. Everything points to a big run

His stablemate Linalene has also shaped with promise both runs so far and holds place claims back from a break.

Dancing Gemini's Doncaster-winning form last time was let down a little bit earlier this week but he still won that very well and has to rate a big and clear main danger. With Group 1-class performers Haatem and Tamfana far from sure to be fully primed, it could be that Cicero's Gift can be something of a surprise package and claim third.
